item.title: Worldview Weekly — September 10, 2026
item.description: Worldview Weekly. September tenth, twenty twenty-six. This week’s issue is organized around a recurring tension in global affairs: the difference between trying to control a system and understanding how the system adapts. That tension appears in manufacturing policy, where governments can move tariffs, subsidies, and supply chains but cannot easily reverse the productivity forces reducing industrial employment. It appears in geopolitics, where sanctions can inflict severe economic pain without necessarily producing political capitulation, and where loose institutions such as BRICS can matter even without becoming coherent alliances.
